tb-3A01-7.question:
An object O is placed at x = 1 between two vertical mirrors M1 and M2 at x = −2 and x = 2 respectively (Fig e). I1 is the image of O formed by M1. I2 is the image of O formed by M2. I3 is the image of I2 formed by M1. Where is I3?

A At x = –3

B At x = –5

C At x = –7

D At x = 5
tb-3A01-7.reasoning:
Distance between I2 and M1

= 3 – (–2) = 5 units

Since object distance equals image distance, I3 is 5 units to the left of M1 (i.e. at x = –7).

tb-3A01-19.question:
Two plane mirrors are facing each other at a right angle. An object O is placed between the mirrors (Fig p). Three images I1, I2 and I3 of O are formed.

(a) Locate I3 in Figure p. (1 mark)

(b) An eye is looking at I2. Two rays which appear to come from I2 enter the eye. By completing the ray diagram, show that the rays come from O after reflection by each mirror in turn. (2 marks) [Hint: You can regard I2 as the image of I1.]

(c) Show that if an incident ray is reflected by both mirrors, the reflected ray is parallel to the incident ray. (3 marks)
tb-3A01-19.answer:
(a) (Correct position of I3) 1A

(b) (Two reflected rays which appear to come from I1) 1A

(Two incident rays from O) 1A

(c) Let i1 and r1 be the angle of incidence and angle of reflection of the first reflection respectively.

Let i2 and r2 be the angle of incidence and angle of reflection of the second reflection respectively.

Suppose i1 = θ .

r1 = i1 = θ

r2 = i2 = 90° – θ 1M

i1 + r1 + i2 + r2

= 2θ + 2(90° – θ) 1M

= 180° 1A

∴ The reflected ray is parallel to the incident ray.

(c) Let θ be the angle of incidence of the first reflection.

The angle of incidence of the second reflection

= 90° – θ 1M

The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray

= 2θ + 2(90° – θ) 1M

= 180° 1A
